equity_bridge.item: Investments in securities (cross-shareholdings and other, balance-sheet carrying value, listed holdings at fair value)
equity_bridge.note: 2026-03-31 FY tanshin p.11 (the H1 balance sheet only shows the aggregate 'investments and other assets' JPY381.7bn). AFS unrealised gains rose JPY6.7bn in H1 FY2027, so the Sept-2026 value is slightly higher. Carried because dividend income (~JPY6bn/yr) is outside the EBITDA-built flows (matching-asset rule).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: FY2027 guidance (+4.9%, H1 +10.6%) decelerating to terminal; the 5-year CAGRs (FYE Mar-2021 -> Mar-2026) start from a COVID trough and the 3-year CAGRs from the FYE Mar-2023 peak (PVC super-cycle, revenue JPY2,809bn), so neither window is a usable trend. The 10-year revenue CAGR of 7.2% brackets a full cycle.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 9.6% vs EPS 5yr 12.3% and revenue 11.4%: within 30%. Equity 3yr CAGR 4.8% is depressed by JPY800bn of buybacks over FYE Mar-2024 to Sept-2026, not by earnings.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF less interest income, JPY m): FY2016 129,587; FY2017 149,884; FY2018 162,936; FY2019 163,492; FY2020 132,179; FY2021 158,788; FY2022 351,043; FY2023 472,071; FY2024 309,746; FY2025 352,365; FY2026 293,774. The owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (-14.6%) is below the reported FCF 3yr CAGR (-10.0%) because interest income grew from JPY16.6bn to JPY62.9bn over the period as rates rose on the ~JPY1.7tn cash pile - a growing share of reported FCF is treasury income, not operations. FYE Mar-2026 owner FCF of JPY294bn is also depressed by capex of JPY356bn (13.8% of revenue) against D&A of JPY243bn.

scenario_narratives.base: Shin-Etsu's two profit engines are at opposite points of their cycles: Electronics Materials (silicon wafers, photoresists, photomask blanks) is at an AI-driven high and carried 54% of FYE Mar-2026 operating income, while Shintech's PVC/chlor-alkali business is in a price trough (segment profit -43% YoY) on Asian export oversupply and soft US housing. The base case has the two partially offset: semiconductor materials growth moderates from the current pace while PVC pricing normalises slowly, so revenue compounds at ~4% and the EBITDA margin settles at the 10-year average of ~35-36% rather than either the FYE Mar-2023 peak (43%) or the FYE Mar-2018 trough (31%). FY2027 guidance (sales JPY2,700bn, OI JPY700bn, EPS JPY286) is treated as a conservative floor given H1 ran +15.6% in operating income. Capex stays elevated (JPY380bn FY2027, plus Shintech Louisiana to 2030) and is charged in full; the JPY1.35tn of net cash and JPY152bn of investment securities are added once in the bridge with their income stripped from the flows.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI data-centre build-out proves multi-year rather than a two-year spike, keeping 300mm wafer and lithography-material volumes and pricing firm while new product lines (TIM, immersion-cooling silicone fluids, QST GaN substrates, optoelectronic substrates) add incremental revenue; Shintech's integrated cost position earns outsized margins once PVC prices recover from 2028; the yen stays weak. Margins return to the 38-39% of the last up-cycle and the company keeps returning >100% of earnings through buybacks, which the flat share count already credits as value-neutral.
scenario_narratives.bear: An AI-capex digestion phase in FYE Mar-2028/29 compounds with a PVC market that does not clear, and the yen strengthens toward 130 against ~79% overseas sales. Revenue falls ~11% over two years, EBITDA margin troughs at 29%, and the mature margin settles at 32.5%. China's heavy rare-earth export controls disrupt the magnet business. The balance sheet (JPY1.75tn cash, Aa3) is never at risk, so this is an earnings and multiple bear case, not a solvency one - which is why the bear value stays well above half the base value.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mid-cycle owner-FCF valuation of a two-engine cyclical. Neither engine's current state is extrapolated: margins anchor on the 10-year average, capex is charged at the guided JPY380bn and tapers only after the Louisiana programme, the JPY1.35tn net cash is added once (interest income stripped), NCI is charged once through a leakage rate, and the terminal multiple is capped at 15x owner FCF as the house cyclical haircut. The result is a value that the market will look through in an AI up-cycle and that the stock has traded well below in PVC/semi troughs (52-week range JPY4,366-7,930).
key_risks_to_valuation: Semiconductor cycle: Electronics Materials is 54% of operating income at an AI-driven high; a capex digestion in 2027-29 is the bear axis.
PVC pricing: Infrastructure Materials profit fell 43% in FYE Mar-2026; recovery timing is unguided and the base case assumes only partial normalisation.
USD/JPY: ~79% of sales overseas (28% US); each JPY10 of yen appreciation is roughly a mid-single-digit hit to yen operating income.

Capex intensity: JPY380bn FY2027 and Shintech's USD3.4bn Louisiana expansion to 2030 mean owner FCF stays well below NOPAT until Y5; if the programme overruns or extends, the capex taper is too optimistic.
Terminal cap: the 15x cap binds in base and bull; using Gordon at 8%/2.5% (18.6x) instead adds roughly JPY600/share to the base case.
Rare-earth supply: China's heavy rare-earth export controls (Jan-2026) affect the magnet business within Electronics Materials.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 4,366-7,930.
data_sources.financials: 4063.T_Metrics.csv (FY2016-FY2026 annual plus Q1/H1 FY2027, JPY millions, post-split share basis); H1 FY2027 tanshin (six months to 2026-09-30) for the balance sheet, share count, cash flow, capex/D&A forecast; FYE Mar-2026 tanshin for investments in securities, NCI profit share and tax; FY2026 integrated report ten-year summary for diluted EPS and interest-bearing debt history.
data_sources.qualitative: 4063.T_Analysis.json (2026-10-31): segment mix, cycle positioning, guidance, bull/bear axes.

inputs.share_count_basis: 1,984,995,865 issued less 169,263,147 treasury = 1,815.73m outstanding at 2026-09-30 (H1 FY2027 tanshin), grossed up 0.08% for share subscription rights (FY2026 basic EPS 252.69 vs diluted 252.49) = 1,817.2m fully diluted. Held FLAT: buybacks (JPY500bn FYE Mar-2026, JPY250bn completed Aug-2026) are already in the Sept-2026 count and net cash; further repurchases are value-neutral in this model.
inputs.sbc_source: unavailable - J-GAAP tanshin and integrated report carry no stock-option expense line. Share subscription rights balance rose JPY7,596m -> 9,190m over H1 FY2027, implying roughly JPY3bn/yr of option expense (~0.1% of revenue); treated as immaterial and modelled at 0%. Valuation overstated by at most ~JPY2/share on this account.
inputs.buyback_note: JPY500,006m purchases of treasury stock in FYE Mar-2026 (cash flow statement) plus JPY250,002m in H1 FY2027 (45.0m shares, authorisation completed Aug-2026). Part-funded by JPY390bn of new long-term borrowings since Mar-2025, which is why total_debt rose from JPY17bn to JPY402bn while cash held at ~JPY1.75tn.
inputs.fy0_note: FY0 = CSV row FY2026 = fiscal year ended 2026-03-31 (company calls it FY2025). Year 1 of the projection = FYE 2027-03-31, the current guidance year.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-30T06:30:00Z (TSE regular close 15:30 JST; Yahoo chart API)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the flows: 10y JGB ~1.7% (Oct-2026) + beta ~1.1 x JPY ERP 5.5% = cost of equity ~7.8%; debt is ~4% of capital at ~1% pre-tax, giving a WACC of ~7.5%. Rounded up to 8.0%, which matches management's own stated ~8% cost of capital (integrated report FY2026, ROE 10.4% / ROIC 14.6% 'above the ~8% cost of capital'). Below the ~9% house reference for JPY keiretsu industrials because of Aa3 credit, JPY1.35tn net cash and global No.1 positions; the cyclical risk is charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate, and the same 8.0% is used in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: None required. J-GAAP filer: operating leases are expensed inside cost of sales/SG&A, no right-of-use assets or lease liabilities are on the balance sheet, and total_debt (JPY4,163m short-term + JPY397,437m long-term borrowings at 2026-09-30) is borrowings only.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows: non-controlling interests (JPY175.8bn book at 2026-09-30; NCI share of net income JPY46.1bn FYE Mar-2025, JPY31.8bn FYE Mar-2026, JPY14.0bn H1 FY2027 = 3.6-6.2% of operating income) are folded into cash_tax_rate_path as a 4.5pp leakage on top of the ~29% cash tax rate (FYE Mar-2026: JPY208,932m tax paid / JPY708,488m pre-tax = 29.5%; P&L effective 28.5%). No NCI deduction in the bridge. Calibration: FY0 EBIT JPY635,204m x (1 - 0.335) = JPY422.4bn vs attributable net income JPY474.5bn less after-tax interest income (~JPY44bn) and securities gains (~JPY7bn) = ~JPY423bn. Ties.
inputs.interest_income_note: JPY62,927m FYE Mar-2026 interest income stripped from the FCF base (net cash JPY1.35tn is ~4.6x owner FCF). The cash pile is added back once, in net_debt. Dividend income (~JPY6bn/yr) is non-operating and never enters the EBITDA-built flows, so its source asset - investments in securities - is carried in equity_bridge.
inputs.working_capital_note: Manufacturer: receivables JPY633bn + inventories JPY816bn + other current JPY107bn less payables JPY193bn, accrued tax JPY104bn and other current liabilities JPY307bn = ~JPY950bn net operating working capital, ~36% of revenue. wc_capture_pct is therefore NEGATIVE (-35): growth consumes cash.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (engine route), routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' with owner-fcf-adaptations.md read in full. Shin-Etsu is a two-engine cyclical: Electronics Materials (silicon wafers, lithography materials; ~54% of FYE Mar-2026 operating income, at an AI-driven cycle high) and Infrastructure Materials (Shintech PVC/chlor-alkali; ~26% of profit, in a price trough after a 43% YoY profit fall). Both are modelled through one EBITDA-margin path anchored on the 10-year average margin of 35.7% (range 26.8%-43.1%), rather than extrapolating either engine's current state. Capex reflects the FY2027 'Investments' forecast of JPY380bn (H1 tanshin p.16) and Shintech's USD3.4bn Louisiana feedstock expansion running to 2030, tapering to ~11% of revenue (vs ~10% D&A) once that programme completes. Historical CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less interest income; SBC nil). Currency: JPY flows, JPY quote, no FX bridge. SBC-zero market: house and street bases coincide, band_position is null by construction. Terminal cap 15x owner FCF (house rule 12-15x for cyclicals) binds in base and bull against a Gordon multiple of 18.6x at 8%/2.5%; the cap is a deliberate cyclical haircut of roughly JPY600/share on the base case.

bear.rationale: FY2027 lands near guidance, then an AI-capex digestion in FYE Mar-2028/29 cuts wafer volumes and pricing (semiconductor materials cycles historically correct 15-25% peak to trough), PVC stays oversupplied with US housing soft, and the yen appreciates toward 130, so revenue falls ~11% over two years and EBITDA margin drops to 29% (the FYE Mar-2017/18 level was 27-31%). Recovery to a 32.5% mature margin, below the 10-year average; a lower terminal cap (13x) and 2.0% growth for a business the market has re-rated as a commodity cyclical.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 +6.0%: guidance is JPY2,700bn (+4.9%) maintained at H1, but H1 ran +10.6% and the implied H2 is flat YoY, which is Shin-Etsu's usual conservatism; 6% allows some H2 yen strength. Then decelerates 5.5% -> 2.5% through the AI build-out and a gradual PVC price normalisation; the 10-year path compounds revenue to ~JPY3.8tn, a 4.0% CAGR vs the 7.2% trailing 10-year CAGR.
base.margin_rationale: Y1 35.0% = guidance OI JPY700bn + D&A JPY240bn on JPY2,700bn (34.8%); H1 actual was 35.3%. Mid-path 36% is the 10-year average EBITDA margin (35.7%, FYE Mar-2017 to Mar-2026) - partial PVC recovery offsetting an eventual semiconductor plateau - fading to 35% mature.
base.capex_rationale: Y1-2 14.0% = FY2027 investment forecast JPY380bn on ~JPY2.73tn. Shintech Louisiana (USD3.4bn to 2030) keeps capex 13-14% through Y4, then tapers to 11% of revenue vs 10% D&A (net growth capex consistent with 2.5% terminal growth).
base.tax_rationale: 29% cash tax (FYE Mar-2026 cash tax paid 29.5% of pre-tax; P&L effective 28.5%; Japan statutory 30.6%, US federal+Louisiana ~25%) plus 4.5pp NCI leakage (3.6-6.2% of operating income over the last three periods) = 33.5% combined, applied to EBIT.

bull.rationale: AI/data-centre wafer and lithography demand sustains high-single-digit volume growth to 2030 (Isesaki Campus, 300mm wafer pricing, TIM/immersion fluids, QST substrates), PVC prices recover from 2028 as Asian export oversupply clears and US housing turns, and USD/JPY stays near 150. Margins return to the FYE Mar-2022 to Mar-2025 band (38-41%) and settle at 37.5%, the level of the last up-cycle's trough year.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 house default. Bear raised to 25% because the larger profit engine (Electronics Materials) is at a cyclical high driven by AI capex, and semiconductor-materials cycles have historically corrected sharply; the bear case is a cyclical earnings drawdown, not a solvency event, so it is not pushed higher. Bull cut to 25% because it needs three independent things to hold at once - AI demand persisting through 2030, a PVC price recovery, and a weak yen.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
